comments.author: @SemperFi4evr
comments.text: Same thing happened to me, but you don't have to pay the subscription if you buy original HP cartridges, which is bullshit because after market cartridges work fine, but they don't have the HP code in them so the printer won't recognize them since the last firmware updates. Also the last update placed your printer into a loop that requires your printer to be connected to the Internet in order to function. So they have pretty much fucked everyone. Best thing to do is buy a tank fed printer as they can't do that on those also if you have your printer on your local network set a rule in your network setting preventing the printer from accessing the internet. And turn off auto updates. The best thing is to stay away from HP, Epson and Canon. Specifically HP, they are the only ATM that locks out your printer if you cancel your subscription and don't install Epson cartridges.  If you purchased an HP+ (e-series) printer model, you have basically agreed to a lifetime requirement to keep the printer connected to the internet and to use only genuine HP chips, which aggressively blocks third-party or generic ink cartridge alternatives through firmware updates. If you purchased a HP "e" series printer throw it away and buy an ink tank system printer there are many available for a decent price. Also if you have a HP Disable Web Services: On the printer's touchscreen menu, go to Settings > Web Services > Remove Web Services. This severs the connection to the HP cloud and completely stops the printer from prompting you to re-enroll. But with tank fed printers you also have a waste ink or maintenance box that has to be changed every so often, the printers are programmed to lock up after a specific number of prints and will not work until the maintenance box is replaced and reset. Usually cost from $20 to $40 depending on the model, but at least you can use aftermarket inks. Simply changing the physical sponge will not unlock the printer. The digital internal counter must be reset. For user-replaceable maintenance boxes, the box comes with a built-in microchip that auto-resets the printer when installed. For older or cheaper models, you have to use third-party software programs (such as the WIC Reset Utility) to digitally reset the internal memory counter back to zero. They have realized that the money is in the ink and they have instigated measures to prevent us from using whatever ink we wish to use. The only way they will stop and begin to treat customers with any semblance of respect is if we just stop buying their products. Don't just cancel and stop purchasing their product but make sure to send emails to their billing department telling them that you intend to stop using their products. And also spread the word to friends and family.
